name: King's Pawn Opening
moves: e4
description: The most popular first move in chess. 1.e4 grabs the center, opens lines for the queen and the light-squared bishop, and usually leads to open, tactical games.
ideas: Occupy the center with a pawn
Open diagonals for the queen and the f1 bishop
Follow up with Nf3, Bc4/Bb5 and quick castling
traps: Beginners often bring the queen out early with Qh5 — it can be chased around with tempo

name: Queen's Pawn Opening
moves: d4
description: 1.d4 claims the center with a pawn that is already protected by the queen. Games tend to be more strategic and closed than after 1.e4.
ideas: Prepare c4 to attack Black's center from the side
traps: The Englund Gambit (1...e5) hides the trap 2.dxe5 Nc6 3.Nf3 Qe7 4.Bf4? Qb4+ winning b2

name: English Opening
moves: c4
description: A flexible flank opening: White controls d5 with the c-pawn and often fianchettoes the king's bishop. It can transpose into many d4 openings.
ideas: Keep options open to transpose into Queen's Gambit structures

name: Réti Opening
moves: Nf3
description: A hypermodern start: White develops a knight, controls the center from a distance and waits to see Black's setup before committing pawns.
ideas: Control e5 and d4 with a piece
Stay flexible: c4, g3, b3 are all possible
Transpose into a favorable d4 or c4 system

name: Bird's Opening
moves: f4
description: 1.f4 fights for e5 and prepares a kingside attack, like a Dutch Defense with an extra tempo. It slightly weakens White's king.
ideas: Fianchetto the queen's bishop with b3 and Bb2
Attack on the kingside with Qe1-h4
traps: From's Gambit: 1...e5 2.fxe5 d6 3.exd6 Bxd6 4.Nc3?? Qh4+ 5.g3 Qxg3+ 6.hxg3 Bxg3# — play 4.Nf3 first

name: Nimzo-Larsen Attack
moves: b3
description: White fianchettoes the queen's bishop immediately to aim it at the long diagonal and the e5 square. A favorite of Bent Larsen and modern speed players.
ideas: Pressure e5 and the long a1-h8 diagonal
Play e3, Nf3 and c4 later

name: King's Fianchetto Opening
moves: g3
description: Also called the Benko Opening. White prepares Bg2 to control the long diagonal and keeps every central option open.
ideas: Choose a central setup later (c4, d4 or e4)

name: Polish Opening
moves: b4
description: The Sokolsky or Orangutan: White gains queenside space and prepares Bb2 to hit e5. Black can attack the b4 pawn directly.
ideas: Follow with a3 or c3 to support b4
traps: After 1...e5 2.Bb2 Bxb4 the pawn is gone — White gets the e5 pawn in return with 3.Bxe5

name: Grob Opening
moves: g4
description: An aggressive but dubious first move that opens the long diagonal for Bg2 while weakening White's kingside.
ideas: Fianchetto with Bg2 and pressure b7
Play for tricks along the h1-a8 diagonal
traps: After 1...d5 2.Bg2 Bxg4 3.c4 c6 4.cxd5 cxd5 5.Qb3 White hits b7 and d5 — but objectively Black is fine
Fool's mate risk: g4 and f3/f4 together allow Qh4#

name: Van Geet Opening
moves: Nc3
description: Also called the Dunst Opening. White develops a knight toward the center and keeps e4 and d4 in reserve.

name: Anderssen's Opening
moves: a3
description: A waiting move used by Adolf Anderssen: White effectively plays Black's openings with an extra tempo a3.
ideas: Play reversed openings with an extra tempo

name: Ware Opening
moves: a4
description: A rare rook-pawn move that does little for the center. White may follow with Ra3 rook lifts, but the move is mostly a surprise weapon.
ideas: Prepare an early Ra3 rook lift

name: Clemenz Opening
moves: h3
description: A quiet waiting move. It prevents ...Bg4 but gives Black a free hand in the center.
ideas: Transpose into a normal setup later

name: Desprez Opening
moves: h4
description: The Kádas Opening: a flank pawn move that prepares a rook lift via h3 but does nothing for the center.

name: Saragossa Opening
moves: c3
description: White prepares d4 and opens the d1-a4 diagonal for the queen. It is solid but passive.

name: Mieses Opening
moves: d3
description: A modest move that opens the c1 bishop and often heads for a King's Indian Attack setup.
ideas: Play e4, Nf3, g3, Bg2 later
Keep the position closed and flexible

name: Van't Kruijs Opening
moves: e3
description: A quiet move that opens lines for the f1 bishop and queen. It can transpose into reversed French or Queen's Pawn systems.

name: Barnes Opening
moves: f3
description: One of the worst first moves: it takes f3 from the knight and weakens the king. It is the first step of Fool's Mate.
traps: Fool's Mate: 1.f3 e5 2.g4?? Qh4# — the fastest checkmate in chess

name: Durkin Opening
moves: Na3
description: The Sodium Attack: White develops the knight to the rim, intending Nc4 or c3/Nc2 later.
ideas: Reroute the knight to c4 or c2
traps: "A knight on the rim is dim" — don't leave it on a3

name: Amar Opening
moves: Nh3
description: The Paris Opening: the knight develops to the edge, heading for f4 or g5. Rarely seen in serious play.

name: King's Pawn Game: Open Game
moves: e4 e5
description: Black mirrors White's first move and claims an equal share of the center. This leads to classical, open positions with lots of piece play.
ideas: Watch out for attacks on f7
traps: Scholar's Mate: 2.Qh5 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6?? 4.Qxf7#

name: Parham Attack (Wayward Queen)
moves: e4 e5 Qh5
description: White brings the queen out immediately, eyeing e5 and f7 and hoping for Scholar's Mate. Against careful play the queen just gets chased.
ideas: Threaten Qxe5+ and Bc4 with Qxf7#
Be ready to retreat the queen
traps: Scholar's Mate: 2...Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6?? 4.Qxf7#
Correct defense: 2...Nc6 3.Bc4 g6 4.Qf3 Nf6 and Black gains time on the queen

name: Center Game
moves: e4 e5 d4 exd4 Qxd4
description: White recaptures on d4 with the queen, which is exposed to ...Nc6 with tempo. It leads to unusual positions where White often castles queenside.
ideas: Attack quickly with f4 and e5
traps: After 3...Nc6 the queen must move — don't put it where ...Nb4 or ...Bb4 hits again

name: Danish Gambit
moves: e4 e5 d4 exd4 c3 dxc3 Bc4 cxb2 Bxb2
description: White sacrifices two pawns for two bishops raking the board and a huge lead in development. Very dangerous at club level.
ideas: Two bishops aimed at f7 and g7
traps: Black's safest antidote: 5...d5! 6.Bxd5 Nf6, giving back a pawn to catch up in development

name: Scotch Game
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4
description: White breaks open the center at once with 3.d4. The play is open and direct, with less theory than the Ruy Lopez.
traps: 4...Nxd4?! 5.Qxd4 just centralizes White's queen
4...Qh4!? (Steinitz) grabs e4 if White is careless

name: Scotch Game: Classical Variation
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Bc5
description: Black attacks the d4 knight at once. White usually plays 5.Be3 or 5.Nxc6, and the play revolves around the a7-g1 diagonal.
ideas: White's Nb3 gains time on the c5 bishop

name: Scotch Game: Mieses Variation
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nxc6 bxc6 e5 Qe7 Qe2 Nd5 c4
description: The modern main line of the Scotch: White gains space with e5 and c4, while Black's queen and bishop are temporarily awkward.
ideas: Doubled c-pawns give Black open b-file
traps: 7...Ba6 pins the c4 pawn — White must watch b3/Qe4 tactics

name: Scotch Gambit
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Bc4
description: Instead of recapturing, White develops the bishop toward f7 and offers a pawn for development. It often transposes to the Two Knights.
ideas: Push e5 to kick a knight on f6
traps: 4...Nf6 5.e5 d5! is Black's cleanest reply — passive defense lets White attack f7

name: Göring Gambit
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 c3
description: A Danish-style gambit inside the Scotch: White offers the c-pawn for rapid development and attacking chances.
ideas: Play for a quick attack on f7
traps: Black can decline with 4...d5! 5.exd5 Qxd5 and stays solid

name: Ponziani Opening
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 c3
description: White prepares d4 with c3, building a classical center. Black can counter directly with ...d5 or ...Nf6.
ideas: Build a big center with d4
Qa4 ideas pinning the c6 knight
traps: 3...Nf6 4.d4 Nxe4 5.d5 Ne7 6.Nxe5 Ng6 leads to sharp play — know it before you try it

name: Italian Game
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4
description: One of the oldest openings. White develops quickly and aims the bishop at Black's weakest square, f7.
ideas: Prepare d4 with c3 to build a strong center
traps: Fried Liver Attack after 3...Nf6 4.Ng5
Légal-style traps after ...Bg4 and an early Nxe5

name: Giuoco Piano
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5
description: The 'quiet game': both sides develop bishops to their best diagonals. White chooses between slow d3 setups and the sharp c3-d4 break.
ideas: Both bishops eye the opponent's f-pawn
c3 and d4 for a big center
Castle quickly and bring rooks to the center
traps: Jerome Gambit 4.Bxf7+? is unsound but tricky

name: Giuoco Pianissimo
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 d3
description: The modern way to play the Italian: White keeps the tension with d3, c3, O-O, Re1 and a slow maneuvering game, as top players do today.
ideas: Slow buildup: c3, O-O, Re1, Nbd2-f1-g3
Prepare d4 at the right moment
Use a4 to make room for the bishop on a2
traps: Watch ...Ng4 hitting f2 if White castles early without h3

name: Giuoco Piano: Main Line
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d4 exd4 cxd4 Bb4+
description: The classical main line: White builds the ideal center with c3 and d4, and Black hits back with a check and pressure on e4.
ideas: Simplify with Bd2 for a safe edge
traps: 7.Nc3 Nxe4 8.O-O enters the Møller Attack
7.Bd2 Bxd2+ 8.Nbxd2 d5! frees Black's game

name: Giuoco Piano: Møller Attack
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d4 exd4 cxd4 Bb4+ Nc3 Nxe4 O-O Bxc3 d5
description: A wild gambit where White sacrifices material to open lines against Black's uncastled king. Precise defense is required from both sides.
ideas: Open the e-file against Black's king
Black should return material with ...Bf6 and ...Ne7
traps: 9...Bf6 10.Re1 Ne7 11.Rxe4 d6 is the known defense; other moves can lose quickly

name: Evans Gambit
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4
description: White sacrifices the b-pawn to gain time for c3 and d4. A favorite of Morphy and Kasparov, it leads to rapid attacks.
ideas: Deflect the c5 bishop with b4
Gain tempo for c3 and d4
Attack f7 with Qb3 and Bc4
traps: Black's ...Bxb4 ...Ba5 must be followed by accurate ...d6 or ...Nf6 lines
Watch Qb3 double attacks on f7 and b7

name: Evans Gambit Accepted
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4 Bxb4 c3 Ba5 d4
description: Black grabs the pawn and White immediately strikes in the center with d4. The c3-pawn and bishop on c4 create strong attacking chances.
ideas: Strong center after c3 and d4
Black aims to return the pawn with ...d6 or ...exd4
traps: 5...Ba5 6.d4 exd4? 7.O-O dxc3?! 8.Qb3 gives White a famous attack

name: Two Knights Defense
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6
description: Black counterattacks e4 instead of copying White. It invites the aggressive 4.Ng5, leading to sharp tactical play.
ideas: Be ready for the Ng5 attack on f7
traps: 4.Ng5 d5 5.exd5 Nxd5? 6.Nxf7! is the Fried Liver Attack
4.Ng5 Bc5!? is the Traxler counterattack

name: Italian Game: Two Knights, d3 Variation
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3
description: White calmly defends e4 and keeps a slow Italian setup. This avoids sharp theory and leads to maneuvering middlegames.
traps: Black's ...Ng4 tricks against f2 must be watched

name: Fried Liver Attack
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5 Nxd5 Nxf7
description: White sacrifices a knight on f7 to drag Black's king into the open. Very dangerous for beginners and great fun to learn.
ideas: Sacrifice on f7 to expose the king
Qf3+ forks king and d5 knight
Bring every piece into the attack
traps: 6...Kxf7 7.Qf3+ Ke6 8.Nc3 — Black's king is stuck in the center
Black avoids it with 5...Na5! instead of 5...Nxd5

name: Two Knights Defense: Polerio Defense
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5 Na5
description: The main line against 4.Ng5: Black gives up a pawn but chases the c4 bishop and gains a big lead in development.
traps: 6.Bb5+ c6 7.dxc6 bxc6 8.Be2 h6 9.Nf3 e4 — Black's activity compensates the pawn

name: Two Knights Defense: Traxler Counterattack
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Bc5
description: Black ignores the threat to f7 and counterattacks f2. A wild, tactical line where both kings come under fire.
traps: 5.Nxf7 Bxf2+! 6.Kxf2 Nxe4+ is the critical line
5.Bxf7+ Ke7 is the safer test for White

name: Hungarian Defense
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Be7
description: A solid but passive answer to the Italian. Black avoids all gambits and prepares ...d6 and ...Nf6.
traps: 4.d4 exd4? 5.c3 gives White a quick initiative

name: Blackburne Shilling Gambit
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nd4
description: A trappy move that invites 4.Nxe5?, which runs into a quick mate. Against correct play it is simply weak.
ideas: Queen to g5 hitting g2 and the knight
traps: 4.Nxe5? Qg5! 5.Nxf7?? Qxg2 6.Rf1 Qxe4+ 7.Be2 Nf3# — smothered-style mate
Correct for White: 4.Nxd4 exd4 5.c3 or 4.O-O

name: Rousseau Gambit
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 f5
description: An aggressive reply where Black strikes at e4 with the f-pawn, opening the f-file and weakening the king.
traps: 4.d3 Nf6 5.Ng5 targets the weakened light squares

name: Jerome Gambit
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 Bxf7+
description: An unsound 19th-century sacrifice: White gives a bishop to drag the king out. Fun in blitz, losing against good defense.
traps: 4...Kxf7 5.Nxe5+ Nxe5 6.Qh5+ g6! 7.Qxe5 d6 and Black is clearly better

name: Ruy Lopez
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5
description: The Spanish Game: White pressures the knight that defends e5 and plays for a long-term edge.
ideas: Castle and play Re1, c3 and d4
traps: Noah's Ark Trap traps the b3 bishop with ...c5-c4
Don't win the e5 pawn too early: Bxc6 + Nxe5 allows ...Qd4

name: Ruy Lopez: Morphy Defense
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4
description: Black asks the bishop's intentions with ...a6. White keeps the pin by retreating to a4, the gateway to most Ruy Lopez main lines.
ideas: Keep the option of breaking the pin
traps: Noah's Ark Trap: White's bishop on b3 can be caught by ...c5 and ...c4

name: Ruy Lopez: Exchange Variation
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Bxc6 dxc6
description: White gives up the bishop pair to damage Black's pawn structure. White aims for a better endgame thanks to the healthy 4-vs-3 kingside majority.
ideas: Trade into an endgame with a kingside majority
Black gets the bishop pair and free development
O-O and d4 are White's main plans
traps: 5.Nxe5? Qd4! wins the pawn back with advantage

name: Ruy Lopez: Berlin Defense
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6
description: The 'Berlin Wall' made famous by Kramnik: an ultra-solid defense that counterattacks e4 and often heads for a queenless middlegame.
ideas: Accept the endgame with the bishop pair

name: Ruy Lopez: Berlin Defense, Berlin Wall
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4 Nd6 Bxc6 dxc6 dxe5 Nf5 Qxd8+ Kxd8
description: The Berlin endgame: queens are traded early, Black has lost castling but holds the bishop pair and a solid fortress-like structure.
ideas: White uses the kingside majority (e5, f4-f5)

name: Ruy Lopez: Berlin Defense, d3 Variation
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 d3
description: White avoids the Berlin endgame by quietly defending e4 with d3, keeping queens on and a slow Spanish-style game.
ideas: Slow buildup with c3, O-O, Re1, Nbd2
Maneuver like in the Closed Ruy

name: Ruy Lopez: Closed
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7
description: Black develops calmly and prepares to castle, leading to the Closed Ruy — a rich, strategic battle with maneuvering on both wings.
traps: After 6.Re1 b5 7.Bb3 d6 8.c3 O-O 9.h3 the main line begins; omitting h3 allows ...Bg4

name: Ruy Lopez: Closed, Main Line
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 d6 c3 O-O h3
description: The classical tabiya of the Spanish. Black chooses between Chigorin, Breyer, Zaitsev and other systems.
ideas: White prepares d4 with full support
Black reorganizes queenside pieces before ...c5 or ...d5

name: Ruy Lopez: Closed, Chigorin Defense
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 d6 c3 O-O h3 Na5 Bc2 c5 d4
description: Black kicks the b3 bishop, plays ...c5 and builds queenside space. A classical system with deep strategic content.
ideas: White plays Nbd2-f1-g3 and d5 at the right moment

name: Ruy Lopez: Closed, Breyer Defense
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 d6 c3 O-O h3 Nb8
description: Black retreats the knight to b8 to reroute it to d7, freeing the c-pawn and making room for ...Bb7. Favored by Spassky and Carlsen.

name: Ruy Lopez: Closed, Zaitsev Variation
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 d6 c3 O-O h3 Bb7 d4 Re8
description: Black piles pressure on e4 with ...Bb7 and ...Re8, preparing ...Bf8. A favorite of Karpov in his World Championship matches.
traps: 10.Ng5 Rf8 11.Nf3 Re8 repeats — White must find a different plan to avoid a draw

name: Ruy Lopez: Marshall Attack
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 O-O c3 d5
description: Frank Marshall's famous pawn sacrifice: Black gives a pawn for a dangerous kingside attack. Deeply analyzed and fully sound.
ideas: White must defend precisely and return material
traps: White's greedy Rxe5 lines allow ...Bd6 and ...Qh4 with a ferocious attack

name: Ruy Lopez: Anti-Marshall
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 O-O a4
description: White avoids the Marshall gambit by attacking the b5 pawn with 8.a4, pressuring the queenside instead.

name: Ruy Lopez: Open Variation
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Nxe4
description: Black grabs the e4 pawn and gets active piece play. White regains it with d4 and gets a space advantage with e5.
ideas: White plays d4, dxe5 and c3
traps: The Tarrasch Trap: 6.d4 b5 7.Bb3 d5 8.dxe5 Be6 9.c3 Be7 10.Re1 O-O 11.Nd4 Qd7?? 12.Nxe6 fxe6 13.Rxe4 wins

name: Ruy Lopez: Schliemann Defense
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5
description: The Jaenisch Gambit: Black hits back at e4 with the f-pawn, leading to sharp, King's-Gambit-like positions with colors reversed.
traps: 4.Nc3 fxe4 5.Nxe4 d5 6.Nxe5! dxe4 7.Nxc6 is a long forcing line to know

name: Ruy Lopez: Steinitz Defense
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 d6
description: Black solidly defends e5 with ...d6, but the position is passive and White gets a free hand in the center.
traps: Tarrasch Trap: 4.d4 Bd7 5.Nc3 Nf6 6.O-O Be7 7.Re1 O-O?? 8.Bxc6 Bxc6 9.dxe5 dxe5 10.Qxd8 Raxd8 11.Nxe5 wins a pawn and soon the exchange

name: Ruy Lopez: Classical Defense
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Bc5
description: Black develops the bishop actively to c5, as in the Italian. White usually reacts with c3 and d4.
traps: 4.c3 f5!? is the sharp Cordel Gambit

name: Ruy Lopez: Arkhangelsk Variation
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O b5 Bb3 Bb7
description: Black develops the bishop to b7 early, adding pressure to e4 and the long diagonal. A dynamic alternative to the Closed lines.
ideas: Sharp tactics around e4 and f2

name: Ruy Lopez: Møller Defense
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O b5 Bb3 Bc5
description: Also called the Neo-Arkhangelsk: Black puts the bishop on c5 to pressure f2 and d4.

name: Ruy Lopez: Bird Variation
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nd4
description: Black trades knights to break the pin, accepting a doubled d-pawn. Rare but playable.

name: Petrov's Defense
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6
description: The Russian Game: Black counterattacks e4 instead of defending e5. Extremely solid and a favorite of elite players seeking equality.
traps: 3.Nxe5 Nxe4?? 4.Qe2! Nf6?? 5.Nc6+ wins the queen by discovered attack
Correct: 3.Nxe5 d6 4.Nf3 Nxe4

name: Petrov's Defense: Classical Attack
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nf3 Nxe4 d4
description: The main line of the Petrov. White gains a small space edge while Black's knight on e4 is strong but can be challenged.
ideas: Challenge the e4 knight with Bd3, O-O, Re1, c4

name: Petrov's Defense: Steinitz Attack
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d4
description: White opens the center immediately with 3.d4, leading to more open play than the main line.

name: Stafford Gambit
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6
description: A trappy gambit popular online: Black gives a pawn for quick development and many tricks against the king.
ideas: Lure the knight into taking on c6
traps: 4.Nxc6 dxc6 5.d3?? Bc5 6.Bg5?? Nxe4! 7.Bxd8 Bxf2+ 8.Ke2 Bg4# — the famous mate
Correct for White: 4.Nxc6 dxc6 5.d3 Bc5 6.Be2 and the gambit is weak

name: Philidor Defense
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 d6
description: A solid but passive defense that protects e5 with a pawn. White gets more space, but Black's position is hard to break.
traps: Légal Trap: 3.Bc4 Bg4 4.Nc3 g6? 5.Nxe5! Bxd1?? 6.Bxf7+ Ke7 7.Nd5#
3.d4 exd4 leads to a passive Exchange line

name: Philidor Defense: Hanham Variation
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 Nbd7
description: Black keeps the strongpoint on e5 with ...Nbd7. The resulting position resembles an Old Indian with solid but cramped play.
ideas: Prepare ...b5 or ...exd4 at the right time
traps: 5.Bc4 Be7 6.dxe5 dxe5? 7.Bxf7+! Kxf7 8.Ng5+ Kg8 9.Ne6 wins the queen — recapture 6...Nxe5 instead

name: Philidor Defense: Exchange Variation
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 exd4
description: Black gives up the center to free the pieces. White centralizes with Nxd4 and gets a comfortable space edge.

name: Latvian Gambit
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 f5
description: A very aggressive and risky gambit: Black strikes e4 with the f-pawn at once, weakening the king for activity.
traps: 3.Nxe5 Qf6 4.d4 d6 5.Nc4 fxe4 6.Nc3 Qg6 7.f3! is strong for White
Bc4 ideas against the weakened e8-h5 diagonal

name: Elephant Gambit
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 d5
description: Black strikes back immediately in the center with ...d5. Objectively dubious, but it can confuse unprepared opponents.
traps: 3.exd5 e4 4.Qe2 Nf6 5.d3 and White is better

name: Damiano Defense
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 f6
description: A weak defense of e5 that weakens the king's diagonal. A classic lesson in why ...f6 is dangerous.
ideas: (Not recommended) defend e5 with a pawn
traps: 3.Nxe5! fxe5? 4.Qh5+ Ke7 (4...g6 5.Qxe5+) 5.Qxe5+ Kf7 6.Bc4+ and White wins

name: Four Knights Game
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6
description: A classical and symmetrical opening: both sides develop knights first. Simple principles, good for learning.
traps: 4.Nxe5? Nxe5 5.d4 is the Halloween Gambit — a real knight sacrifice

name: Four Knights Game: Spanish Variation
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6 Bb5
description: White pins the c6 knight like in the Ruy Lopez. Black can mirror with ...Bb4 or play the sharp Rubinstein ...Nd4.
ideas: Castle and play d3 or d4
traps: 4...Nd4 5.Nxe5? Qe7 regains material with interest

name: Four Knights Game: Scotch Variation
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6 d4
description: White opens the center with d4. After 4...exd4 5.Nxd4 play resembles the Scotch Game with both knights developed.

name: Four Knights Game: Halloween Gambit
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6 Nxe5
description: A spooky knight sacrifice: White gives a whole piece for a big pawn center and chasing Black's knights around.
ideas: Big center with d4 and e5
traps: 4...Nxe5 5.d4 Ng6 6.e5 Ng8 7.Bc4 — Black must defend calmly, then is much better

name: Three Knights Game
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3
description: White develops the queen's knight before deciding on a plan. Black usually transposes to the Four Knights with ...Nf6.
ideas: Flexible: Bb5, Bc4 or d4 later

name: Vienna Game
moves: e4 e5 Nc3
description: White develops the queen's knight first, keeping the f-pawn free for an early f4 push. It can be quiet or very aggressive.
ideas: Prepare f4 like a King's Gambit
traps: Frankenstein-Dracula: 2...Nf6 3.Bc4 Nxe4!? 4.Qh5 is very sharp

name: Vienna Game: Falkbeer Variation
moves: e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6
description: Black develops and counterattacks e4. White chooses between the Vienna Gambit (f4), Bc4 or a quiet g3.

name: Vienna Game: Max Lange Defense
moves: e4 e5 Nc3 Nc6
description: Black mirrors White's development. White can still play f4, Bc4 or a slow g3 setup.

name: Vienna Gambit
moves: e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 f4
description: A King's Gambit with the knight already on c3. White aims to open the f-file and push e5 to kick Black's knight.
traps: 3...d5! is the best reply: 4.fxe5 Nxe4 5.Nf3 with complex play
3...exf4 4.e5 Ng8 gives White a big center

name: Vienna Game: Frankenstein-Dracula Variation
moves: e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Qh5 Nd6 Bb3 Nc6 Nb5 g6 Qf3 f5 Qd5 Qe7 Nxc7+ Kd8 Nxa8 b6
description: One of the wildest lines in chess: White wins a rook but the knight on a8 is trapped, and Black gets a powerful center and attack.
ideas: Black sacrifices the exchange for a huge center
White's queen must avoid getting trapped
traps: 4.Qh5 threatens Qxf7# — Black must play 4...Nd6

name: Bishop's Opening
moves: e4 e5 Bc4
description: White develops the bishop first, aiming at f7 and keeping the f-pawn free. It often transposes to the Italian or Vienna.

name: Bishop's Opening: Berlin Defense
moves: e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6
description: Black immediately counterattacks e4. White usually defends with d3 and plays a slow Italian-style game.
traps: 3.d4 exd4 4.Nf3 is the Urusov Gambit — sharp play

name: King's Gambit
moves: e4 e5 f4
description: The romantic gambit of the 19th century: White offers the f-pawn to deflect Black's e-pawn, open the f-file and build a big center.
ideas: Deflect the e5 pawn and play d4
Open the f-file for an attack on f7
traps: After 2...exf4 3.Nf3 g5 4.h4 g4 5.Ne5 (Kieseritzky) White fights for the f4 pawn
Without Nf3, ...Qh4+ forces White's king to move — 3.Nf3 prevents it

name: King's Gambit Accepted
moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4
description: Black takes the pawn. The fight revolves around whether Black can keep the f4 pawn or must return it for development.
ideas: Black can hold the pawn with ...g5
White plays Nf3, d4 and Bxf4
Kings often stay in the center
traps: 3.Nf3 g5 4.Bc4 g4 5.O-O!? gxf3 6.Qxf3 is the Muzio Gambit

name: King's Gambit: Kieseritzky Gambit
moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 g5 h4 g4 Ne5
description: White undermines Black's pawn chain with h4 and posts the knight on e5. One of the most respected King's Gambit lines.
ideas: Knight on e5 hits f7 and g4
Regain f4 with d4 and Bxf4

name: King's Gambit: Muzio Gambit
moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 g5 Bc4 g4 O-O
description: White sacrifices a whole knight to open the f-file against f7. A spectacular romantic line with huge attacking chances.
ideas: Sacrifice the f3 knight for development

name: King's Gambit: Fischer Defense
moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 d6
description: Bobby Fischer's 'refutation': Black prevents Ne5 with ...d6 before playing ...g5 to keep the extra pawn.

name: King's Gambit: Bishop's Gambit
moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Bc4
description: White develops the bishop instead of Nf3, allowing ...Qh4+ but keeping the king active on f1.
ideas: The king walks to f1 safely

name: King's Gambit Declined: Falkbeer Countergambit
moves: e4 e5 f4 d5
description: Black declines with a counter-gambit, striking at the center and opening lines toward White's weakened king.

name: King's Gambit Declined: Classical Variation
moves: e4 e5 f4 Bc5
description: Black ignores the gambit and develops the bishop to c5, preventing White from castling short easily.
traps: 3.fxe5?? Qh4+ 4.g3 Qxe4+ wins the rook on h1

name: Sicilian Defense
moves: e4 c5
description: Black's most popular reply to 1.e4: fight for the d4 square with a flank pawn and create an unbalanced game.
ideas: Trade the c-pawn for White's d-pawn
traps: In many lines White sacrifices on e6, d5 or b5 — watch for knight sacrifices

name: Sicilian Defense: Old Sicilian
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6
description: Black develops the queen's knight to fight for d4. It leads to the Sveshnikov, Classical, Accelerated Dragon or Rossolimo.

name: Sicilian Defense: Modern Variations
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6
description: The most common Sicilian move order: ...d6 prepares ...Nf6 and keeps the Najdorf, Dragon, Classical and Scheveningen possible.

name: Sicilian Defense: French Variation
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6
description: Black plays ...e6, heading for the Kan, Taimanov or Four Knights Sicilian. Flexible and solid.

name: Sicilian Defense: Open
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4
description: White opens the center with d4 and recaptures with the knight. White gets a lead in development; Black gets the half-open c-file and a central pawn majority.

name: Sicilian Defense: Najdorf Variation
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6
description: The most famous Sicilian, played by Fischer and Kasparov. The quiet ...a6 controls b5 and prepares ...e5 or ...e6 with a queenside counterattack.
traps: 6.Bg5 e6 7.f4 Qb6 is the Poisoned Pawn — grabbing b2 is risky but sound
Watch for Nd5 and Bxe6 sacrifices

name: Sicilian Najdorf: English Attack
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Be3 e5 Nb3 Be6 f3
description: White plays Be3, f3, Qd2 and O-O-O, then storms the kingside with g4-g5. A modern, aggressive weapon.

name: Sicilian Najdorf: 6.Bg5
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bg5 e6 f4
description: The classical attack on the Najdorf. White pins the knight and prepares e5 or f5 breaks with a direct assault.
ideas: Push e5 or f5 to break open
traps: 7...Qb6 8.Qd2 Qxb2 is the Poisoned Pawn
7...b5?! 8.e5! dxe5 9.fxe5 Qc7 10.exf6 Qe5+ is the Polugaevsky line

name: Sicilian Najdorf: Poisoned Pawn
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bg5 e6 f4 Qb6 Qd2 Qxb2
description: Black's queen grabs the b2 pawn and must survive a ferocious attack. One of the most heavily analyzed lines in chess.
ideas: The black queen can get trapped — precise moves needed
traps: 9.Rb1 Qa3 10.f5 and 10.e5 are White's main attacking tries

name: Sicilian Najdorf: Opocensky Variation
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Be2 e5
description: White plays the calm 6.Be2 and Black answers with ...e5, leading to a positional battle over the d5 square.
ideas: Black's backward d6 pawn vs. active pieces

name: Sicilian Defense: Dragon Variation
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6
description: Black fianchettoes the king's bishop, creating a powerful 'dragon' on the long diagonal. Leads to razor-sharp opposite-side castling battles.
traps: Watch Bh6 trades — removing the g7 bishop weakens the king
Rxc3 exchange sacrifices are typical for Black

name: Sicilian Dragon: Yugoslav Attack
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3 Bg7 f3 O-O Qd2 Nc6
description: White castles queenside and storms with h4-h5 to open the h-file against the black king. A classic race of attacks.
ideas: Bh6 to trade Black's dragon bishop
traps: Black's ...Rxc3 exchange sacrifice can wreck White's queenside

name: Sicilian Defense: Classical Variation
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6
description: Black develops both knights and keeps all options open. White chooses Richter-Rauzer (Bg5), Sozin (Bc4) or quieter lines.

name: Sicilian Defense: Richter-Rauzer Attack
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 Bg5
description: White pins the f6 knight and plans Qd2 and O-O-O, preventing the Dragon setup and preparing an attack.

name: Sicilian Defense: Sozin Attack
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 Bc4
description: White aims the bishop at e6 and f7, a favorite of Bobby Fischer. Sacrifices on e6 and d5 are common.

name: Sicilian Defense: Scheveningen Variation
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 e6
description: Black sets up a 'small center' with pawns on d6 and e6. Solid but flexible, it was a favorite of Kasparov.
ideas: Pawns on d6/e6 control the center
Wait for the right moment for ...d5 or ...e5
traps: The Keres Attack 6.g4! is the sharpest test

name: Sicilian Scheveningen: Keres Attack
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 e6 g4
description: White throws the g-pawn forward immediately to kick Black's knight and launch a kingside attack.
ideas: Kick the f6 knight with g5

name: Sicilian Defense: Sveshnikov Variation
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 e5 Ndb5 d6
description: Black accepts a hole on d5 and a backward pawn in exchange for dynamic piece play and the bishop pair. A modern main line used by Carlsen.
ideas: Dynamic play vs. the d5 hole
traps: After 8.Bg5 a6 9.Na3 b5 Black must know ...f5 and ...Bg7 plans

name: Sicilian Defense: Kalashnikov Variation
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 e5 Nb5 d6
description: A cousin of the Sveshnikov: Black plays ...e5 before ...Nf6, keeping options for ...Be7 and ...f5.
ideas: Accept the d5 hole for activity

name: Sicilian Defense: Taimanov Variation
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nc6
description: A flexible system: Black develops the knight to c6 and keeps the bishops and d-pawn options open. Popular at the top level.
traps: 5.Nb5 d6 6.c4 enters a Maroczy-like bind

name: Sicilian Taimanov: Main Line
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nc6 Nc3 Qc7 Be3 a6
description: The modern Taimanov tabiya. White often plays Qd2/Qf3 and O-O-O, while Black aims for ...Nf6, ...Bb4 or ...b5.

name: Sicilian Defense: Kan Variation
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 a6
description: The Paulsen/Kan: Black plays ...a6 early to keep maximal flexibility. A hedgehog structure often arises.
traps: 5.Bd3 and c4 create a Maroczy bind — Black must find ...b5 or ...d5 breaks

name: Sicilian Defense: Four Knights Variation
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6
description: Black develops both knights and prepares ...Bb4 to pressure e4. It can transpose to many other Sicilian lines.
traps: 6.Ndb5 Bb4 7.a3 Bxc3+ 8.Nxc3 d5 is the main line

name: Sicilian Defense: Accelerated Dragon
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 g6
description: Black fianchettoes without ...d6, saving a tempo and preparing ...d5 in one go. White's main try is the Maroczy Bind with c4.
ideas: Bishop on g7 eyes the long diagonal
traps: 5.Nc3 Bg7 6.Be3 Nf6 7.Bc4 O-O 8.Bb3 Na5? 9.e5 Ne8 10.Bxf7+! Kxf7 11.Ne6! wins the queen

name: Sicilian Defense: Maroczy Bind
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 g6 c4
description: White grips d5 with pawns on c4 and e4, restricting Black's counterplay. A strategic, space-gaining setup.

name: Sicilian Defense: Hyperaccelerated Dragon
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 g6
description: Black fianchettoes on move two, keeping maximum flexibility. White can respond with d4 or an early c3.

name: Sicilian Defense: Alapin Variation
moves: e4 c5 c3
description: White prepares d4 to build a full pawn center, avoiding the heavy theory of the Open Sicilian. A favorite anti-Sicilian at all levels.

name: Sicilian Alapin: 2...Nf6
moves: e4 c5 c3 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 cxd4 Nf3
description: Black attacks e4 at once; White gains space with e5 and the knight finds a central home on d5.

name: Sicilian Alapin: 2...d5
moves: e4 c5 c3 d5 exd5 Qxd5 d4
description: Black takes on d5 and the queen centralizes; since c3 took away the knight's square, the queen is safe.

name: Smith-Morra Gambit
moves: e4 c5 d4 cxd4 c3
description: White sacrifices a pawn for a lead in development and open c- and d-files. Very dangerous in club and online play.
ideas: Fast development: Nc3, Nf3, Bc4, O-O, Qe2, Rd1
traps: Siberian Trap: 4.Nxc3 Nc6 5.Nf3 e6 6.Bc4 Qc7 7.O-O Nf6 8.Qe2 Ng4! 9.h3?? Nd4! wins the queen or mates on h2
Black can decline with 3...Nf6 or 3...d3

name: Smith-Morra Gambit Accepted
moves: e4 c5 d4 cxd4 c3 dxc3 Nxc3
description: Black takes the pawn. White's development lead is significant; Black must develop carefully.
ideas: Bc4, Nf3, O-O, Qe2 and Rd1
Pressure on d6 and the c-file
traps: Black's ...d6, ...Nf6, ...e6 setups must watch e5 breaks and Nb5

name: Sicilian Defense: Closed
moves: e4 c5 Nc3
description: White avoids opening the center and plays a slow kingside setup with g3, Bg2, d3, f4. Spassky's favorite.

name: Sicilian Closed: Main Line
moves: e4 c5 Nc3 Nc6 g3 g6 Bg2 Bg7 d3 d6
description: The classic Closed Sicilian position with fianchettoes on both sides. White plays on the kingside, Black on the queenside.
ideas: White: Be3, Qd2, f4 and kingside attack

name: Sicilian Defense: Grand Prix Attack
moves: e4 c5 Nc3 Nc6 f4
description: White plays an early f4 and develops the bishop to c4 or b5, aiming for a direct kingside attack. Popular in club play.

name: Sicilian Defense: Rossolimo Variation
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5
description: White develops the bishop to b5 to pin the knight and often doubles Black's pawns with Bxc6. A solid anti-Sicilian.
ideas: Pin and maybe take on c6

name: Sicilian Defense: Moscow Variation
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 Bb5+
description: White gives check with the bishop to simplify, avoiding the Najdorf and Dragon. Often bishops are traded on d7.

name: Sicilian Defense: O'Kelly Variation
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 a6
description: Black plays ...a6 on move two to keep options open and set traps against natural moves like 3.d4.
ideas: After 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nf6 Black hits e4
traps: 3.c3! is the best answer

name: Sicilian Defense: Nimzowitsch Variation
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nf6
description: Black attacks e4 like the Alekhine Defense. After 3.e5 Nd5 play resembles an Alekhine with ...c5 inserted.
traps: 3.e5 Nd5 4.Nc3 e6 5.Nxd5 exd5 6.d4 gives White a nice edge

name: Sicilian Defense: Wing Gambit
moves: e4 c5 b4
description: White sacrifices the b-pawn to deflect the c5 pawn and build a center with d4. Rare and dubious.

name: French Defense
moves: e4 e6
description: A solid defense where Black prepares ...d5 and challenges White's center. Black's light-squared bishop is often a problem piece.
traps: The light-squared bishop on c8 can become 'bad' behind the e6 pawn

name: French Defense: King's Indian Attack
moves: e4 e6 d3
description: White avoids French theory with a King's Indian setup: d3, Nd2, Ngf3, g3, Bg2, O-O, and a kingside attack with e5.
ideas: Push e5 to gain kingside space

name: French Defense: Advance Variation
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5
description: White locks the center with e5, gaining space on the kingside. Black attacks the chain base with ...c5 and ...Qb6.
ideas: Defend d4 with c3 and Nf3
traps: Black's queen grab on d4 can lose to Bb5+ tactics
Milner-Barry Gambit sacrifices d4 for development

name: French Advance: Milner-Barry Gambit
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6 Bd3 cxd4 cxd4 Bd7 O-O Nxd4 Nxd4 Qxd4 Nc3
description: White sacrifices the d4 pawn for rapid development and a dangerous attack against Black's uncastled king.
ideas: Keep Black's king in the center
traps: 10...Qxe5?? 11.Re1 Qb8 12.Nxd5! with a crushing attack

name: French Defense: Exchange Variation
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 exd5 exd5
description: White releases the tension with a symmetrical pawn structure. Simple and solid, though often drawish.

name: French Defense: Tarrasch Variation
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2
description: White develops the knight to d2, avoiding the Winawer pin. Black usually replies ...c5 or ...Nf6.
ideas: Keep c3 available for the pawn

name: French Tarrasch: Open Variation
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2 c5
description: Black strikes at d4 immediately, often accepting an isolated queen's pawn in exchange for active pieces.

name: French Tarrasch: Closed Variation
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2 Nf6 e5 Nfd7
description: White gains space with e5 and supports d4 with c3; Black attacks the chain with ...c5 and ...f6.

name: French Defense: Rubinstein Variation
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4
description: Black gives up the center to get free development. Solid but passive; White gets a small, lasting edge.

name: French Defense: Paulsen Variation
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3
description: The main line move: White defends e4 with the knight. Black chooses between the Winawer (...Bb4), Classical (...Nf6) and Rubinstein (...dxe4).

name: French Defense: Winawer Variation
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4
description: Black pins the c3 knight and often gives up the bishop for it, damaging White's pawns. Very sharp and strategically complex.
traps: After 7.Qg4 Black must choose between ...O-O and the sharp ...Qc7 pawn sacrifice

name: French Winawer: Main Line
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5 a3 Bxc3+ bxc3
description: The main Winawer structure: White has the bishop pair and kingside space, Black has better structure and queenside play.

name: French Defense: Classical Variation
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6
description: Black develops the knight and attacks e4. White chooses Bg5 (classical), e5 (Steinitz) or other plans.

name: French Defense: Steinitz Variation
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6 e5 Nfd7 f4
description: White gains space with e5 and supports it with f4, building a broad pawn chain and preparing a kingside attack.

name: French Defense: MacCutcheon Variation
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Bb4
description: Black counter-pins the c3 knight instead of breaking the pin, leading to sharp and unbalanced play.

name: French Classical: Main Line
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e5 Nfd7 Bxe7 Qxe7
description: White trades dark-squared bishops and keeps the e5 space advantage. Black plays ...c5 and ...a6 for queenside play.

name: Caro-Kann Defense
moves: e4 c6
description: A rock-solid defense: Black prepares ...d5 while keeping the light-squared bishop free. Great for players who like safe, structured positions.
ideas: Develop the bishop outside the pawn chain
traps: Smothered mate: 3.Nc3 dxe4 4.Nxe4 Nd7 5.Qe2 Ngf6?? 6.Nd6#

name: Caro-Kann: Advance Variation
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5
description: White grabs space with e5. Black develops the bishop to f5 and attacks the chain with ...c5 or ...e6 and ...c5.

name: Caro-Kann Advance: Short Variation
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nf3 e6 Be2
description: Nigel Short's quiet system: White develops calmly, castles and aims for c4 or slow pressure. Low risk, steady edge.

name: Caro-Kann: Classical Variation
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5
description: Black develops the bishop with tempo on the knight. A classical and very solid main line, also reached via 3.Nd2.
traps: After 6.Ng3 Bg6 7.h4, Black plays 7...h6 so the bishop can retreat to h7 when h5 comes

name: Caro-Kann Classical: Main Line
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4 h6 Nf3 Nd7 h5 Bh7 Bd3 Bxd3 Qxd3
description: The classical tabiya: White's h5 pawn grabs kingside space while Black has a sound structure.

name: Caro-Kann: Karpov Variation
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nd7
description: Black prepares ...Ngf6 so that the e4 knight can be traded without doubled pawns. Very solid; Karpov's favorite.
traps: 5.Qe2 Ngf6?? 6.Nd6# — the famous smothered mate
5.Ng5 Ngf6 6.Bd3 e6 7.N1f3 h6? 8.Nxe6! is a known sacrifice

name: Caro-Kann: Bronstein-Larsen Variation
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf6 Nxf6+ gxf6
description: Black accepts doubled pawns to open the g-file for attacking chances. Dynamic and risky.

name: Caro-Kann: Exchange Variation
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bd3
description: White trades on d5 and develops the bishop to d3 for kingside play. Resembles a Queen's Gambit Declined Exchange with colors reversed.

name: Caro-Kann: Panov-Botvinnik Attack
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4
description: White attacks d5 with c4, often leading to isolated queen's pawn positions with active piece play.

name: Caro-Kann: Two Knights Attack
moves: e4 c6 Nc3 d5 Nf3
description: White develops both knights before d4, keeping options flexible and avoiding main lines.

name: Caro-Kann: Fantasy Variation
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3
description: White supports e4 with the f-pawn, keeping a big center and sometimes gambiting. Sharp and offbeat.

name: Scandinavian Defense
moves: e4 d5
description: Black immediately challenges e4. The queen recaptures on d5 early, but the simple structure makes it easy to learn.
traps: After 2...Qxd5 3.Nc3 the queen must move with tempo loss — choose a safe square

name: Scandinavian Defense: Main Line (Qa5)
moves: e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qa5
description: The classical Scandinavian: the queen goes to a5, pinning the c3 knight and staying active.
ideas: Pin the c3 knight from a5
traps: Watch Bd2 + Nd5 discovered attacks on the a5 queen
b4 tricks can trap the queen

name: Scandinavian Defense: Gubinsky-Melts (Qd6)
moves: e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qd6
description: A modern queen placement: on d6 the queen is centralized and supports ...a6 and ...Nf6 setups.
ideas: Queen on d6 controls central squares
traps: Nb5 hits the queen and c7 — ...a6 or ...c6 is often needed

name: Scandinavian Defense: Qd8 Variation
moves: e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qd8
description: The queen retreats home — the safest square. Black is solid but a bit passive.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Modern Variation
moves: e4 d5 exd5 Nf6
description: Black recaptures with the knight instead of the queen, or gambits the pawn for development.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Portuguese Gambit
moves: e4 d5 exd5 Nf6 d4 Bg4
description: Black gives up the d5 pawn for rapid development and attacking chances against White's queenside.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Icelandic-Palme Gambit
moves: e4 d5 exd5 Nf6 c4 e6
description: Black sacrifices a pawn for a big lead in development. Sharp and aggressive.

name: Pirc Defense
moves: e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6
description: A hypermodern defense: Black lets White build a big center, then attacks it with pieces and ...e5 or ...c5.
traps: The 150 Attack (Be3, Qd2, Bh6) is a dangerous plan for White

name: Pirc Defense: Austrian Attack
moves: e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 f4
description: White builds a massive center with f4, aiming for e5 and a kingside attack. The sharpest answer to the Pirc.
ideas: e5 push to kick the f6 knight

name: Pirc Defense: Classical Variation
moves: e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Nf3 Bg7 Be2
description: White develops naturally and castles. Low-risk play with a lasting central edge.

name: Pirc Defense: 150 Attack
moves: e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3 c6 Qd2
description: White plays Be3, Qd2, Bh6 and h4-h5 — a simple, aggressive plan that's easy to learn.
ideas: Trade the g7 bishop with Bh6

name: Modern Defense
moves: e4 g6
description: Black fianchettoes immediately and delays developing the knight to f6. Very flexible and hypermodern.

name: Modern Defense: Standard Line
moves: e4 g6 d4 Bg7 Nc3 d6
description: The standard Modern setup: Black allows a broad center and waits for the right counterattack with ...c6, ...b5 or ...e5.

name: Alekhine's Defense
moves: e4 Nf6
description: Black provokes White's pawns forward to attack them later. A provocative, hypermodern defense.
traps: The Four Pawns Attack can overrun Black if he is careless

name: Alekhine's Defense: Four Pawns Attack
moves: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6 c4 Nb6 f4
description: White grabs the whole center with four pawns. If it holds, Black is crushed; if not, it becomes a target.

name: Alekhine's Defense: Exchange Variation
moves: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6 c4 Nb6 exd6
description: White releases the tension with exd6, leading to a calmer game with a small space edge.

name: Alekhine's Defense: Modern Variation
moves: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6 Nf3
description: White develops normally instead of chasing the knight. A solid main line with a lasting edge in space.

name: Nimzowitsch Defense
moves: e4 Nc6
description: Black develops the queen's knight to hit d4 and e5, inviting transpositions to 1.e4 e5 or unusual structures.

name: Owen's Defense
moves: e4 b6
description: Black fianchettoes the queen's bishop to pressure e4 from afar.

name: St. George Defense
moves: e4 a6
description: Black plays ...a6 and ...b5 early, made famous by Tony Miles beating world champion Karpov in 1980.

name: Borg Defense
moves: e4 g5
description: A bizarre reply ('Grob' backwards) that weakens Black's kingside for a fianchetto.
traps: 2.d4 h6 3.h4! undermines the g5 pawn

name: Queen's Pawn Game
moves: d4 d5
description: Black mirrors White and keeps a firm grip on the center. The most classical reply to 1.d4.

name: Queen's Pawn Game: Zukertort Variation
moves: d4 d5 Nf3
description: White develops the knight first, keeping options for c4, Bf4 or e3 systems.

name: London System
moves: d4 d5 Bf4
description: A solid system where White plays d4, Bf4, e3, Nf3, c3 and Bd3 against almost anything. Easy to learn and very popular online.
traps: Black's ...c5 and ...Qb6 hitting b2 is the critical test
After Bd3, watch ...Nh5 trying to trade the f4 bishop

name: London System vs. ...Nf6
moves: d4 Nf6 Bf4
description: The London setup against the Indian defenses. White quickly develops the bishop before playing e3.

name: Jobava London System
moves: d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6 Bf4
description: An aggressive London where the knight goes to c3, preparing Nb5, e3 and sometimes queenside castling.
traps: ...a6 often needed to stop Nb5 tricks against c7

name: Colle System
moves: d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 e3
description: A simple system: White plays e3, Bd3, Nbd2, c3, O-O and prepares e4 to open the center for a kingside attack.
ideas: Bishop on d3 aims at h7
traps: The Greek Gift Bxh7+ is a typical Colle attacking pattern

name: Colle-Zukertort System
moves: d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 e3 e6 Bd3 c5 b3
description: White fianchettoes the queen's bishop to b2 while keeping the Colle center. The bishop rakes the long diagonal toward Black's king.

name: Stonewall Attack
moves: d4 d5 e3 Nf6 Bd3
description: White sets up pawns on d4, e3, f4 and c3, then attacks the kingside with Ne5 and Qf3/Rf3.
ideas: Pawns on c3, d4, e3, f4

name: Blackmar-Diemer Gambit
moves: d4 d5 e4 dxe4 Nc3 Nf6 f3
description: White gambits a pawn to open the f-file and speed up development. A favorite of attacking club players.
ideas: Fast development: Nf3, Bd3, O-O, Qe1-h4

name: Richter-Veresov Attack
moves: d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5
description: White develops quickly with Nc3 and Bg5, aiming for f3 and e4. Unusual, aggressive and low on theory.

name: Queen's Gambit
moves: d4 d5 c4
description: White offers the c-pawn to deflect Black's d5 pawn from the center. It's not a real gambit: Black can rarely keep the pawn.
ideas: Build a center with e4 or e3
traps: In the QGA, trying to hold the c4 pawn with ...b5 often loses to a4 and Qf3 tactics

name: Queen's Gambit Accepted
moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4
description: Black takes the c4 pawn, temporarily giving up the center, then hits back with ...c5 and ...e6.
ideas: Don't try to keep the pawn
traps: 3.e3 b5? 4.a4 c6 5.axb5 cxb5 6.Qf3! hits the a8 rook along the long diagonal and wins material

name: Queen's Gambit Accepted: Classical
moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nf3 Nf6 e3 e6 Bxc4 c5 O-O a6
description: The main line: Black lets White recapture and challenges d4 with ...c5. IQP positions are common.

name: Queen's Gambit Accepted: Central Variation
moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e4
description: White builds the full e4/d4 center immediately, then recovers c4. Black counterattacks with ...e5, ...Nf6 or ...c5.

name: Queen's Gambit Declined
moves: d4 d5 c4 e6
description: Black solidly defends d5 with ...e6. One of the most respected defenses in chess, played in many World Championships.
ideas: Free the game with ...c5 or ...dxc4 and ...e5
traps: The Elephant Trap: 4.Bg5 Nbd7 5.cxd5 exd5 6.Nxd5?? Nxd5! 7.Bxd8 Bb4+ 8.Qd2 Bxd2+ 9.Kxd2 Kxd8 wins a piece

name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Normal Defense
moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6
description: The classical QGD position with both knights developed. White picks Bg5, Bf4, cxd5 or Nf3 systems.
traps: Elephant Trap after 4.Bg5 Nbd7 5.cxd5 exd5 6.Nxd5?? Nxd5!

name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Exchange Variation
moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 cxd5 exd5
description: White trades on d5 to fix Black's structure, then plays the famous minority attack with b4-b5.

name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Orthodox Defense
moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e3 O-O Nf3 Nbd7
description: The classical main line of the QGD: solid but somewhat passive. Black waits for the freeing ...c5 or ...dxc4 and ...e5.

name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Tartakower Defense
moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e3 O-O Nf3 h6 Bh4 b6
description: Black fianchettoes the queen's bishop to solve the classic QGD problem piece. Used by Kasparov and Karpov.

name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Lasker Defense
moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e3 O-O Nf3 h6 Bh4 Ne4
description: Black trades pieces with ...Ne4 to relieve the cramped QGD position. Very solid and drawish.
ideas: Trade pieces to free the position

name: QGD: Cambridge Springs Defense
moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Nbd7 e3 c6 Nf3 Qa5
description: Black's queen hits the pinned c3 knight and g5 bishop. Trappy and active.
traps: Careless White play loses a piece to ...dxc4 and ...Ne4
Elephant Trap is possible earlier

name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Ragozin Defense
moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Bb4
description: A Nimzo-Indian-like setup inside the QGD: Black pins the c3 knight for active piece play.

name: Tarrasch Defense
moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 c5
description: Black accepts an isolated queen's pawn for free piece play. Dr. Tarrasch considered it the only correct defense.

name: Semi-Tarrasch Defense
moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 c5 cxd5 Nxd5
description: Black recaptures with the knight to avoid the isolated pawn. White often gets a mobile center with e4.

name: Queen's Gambit Declined: 5.Bf4
moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Be7 Bf4
description: The modern Bf4 system: White develops the bishop outside the pawn chain and often plays e3 and c5 or a slow buildup.
ideas: Pressure on c7 and the queenside

name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Alatortsev Variation
moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Be7
description: Black delays ...Nf6 to avoid the Exchange Variation with Nge2 setups. Subtle move-order play.

name: Albin Countergambit
moves: d4 d5 c4 e5
description: Black sacrifices the e-pawn for a cramping pawn on d4 and rapid development. Trappy and aggressive.
traps: The Lasker Trap: 3.dxe5 d4 4.e3? Bb4+ 5.Bd2 dxe3! 6.Bxb4?? exf2+ 7.Ke2 fxg1=N+! wins

name: Chigorin Defense
moves: d4 d5 c4 Nc6
description: Black develops pieces aggressively instead of building a pawn structure, aiming for piece pressure on d4.

name: Baltic Defense
moves: d4 d5 c4 Bf5
description: Black develops the light-squared bishop before ...e6, solving the classic problem piece of the QGD.
traps: 4.Qb3 hitting b7 is a direct test

name: Slav Defense
moves: d4 d5 c4 c6
description: Black defends d5 with ...c6, keeping the c8 bishop free. Solid and dynamic, played by many world champions.
ideas: Develop the bishop to f5 or g4

name: Slav Defense: Exchange Variation
moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 cxd5 cxd5
description: White simplifies to a symmetrical structure. Solid and drawish, but White keeps a tiny initiative.

name: Slav Defense: Czech Variation
moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5
description: Black takes on c4 and develops the bishop to f5. White regains the pawn and fights for e4.

name: Slav Defense: Chebanenko Variation
moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 a6
description: The flexible ...a6 Slav: Black prepares ...b5 to gain queenside space and keeps many options.

name: Semi-Slav Defense
moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 e6
description: Combining ...c6 and ...e6, Black builds a solid triangle. It leads to some of the sharpest lines in chess (Meran, Botvinnik).

name: Semi-Slav: Meran Variation
moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 e6 e3 Nbd7 Bd3 dxc4 Bxc4 b5
description: Black takes on c4 and expands with ...b5, gaining time and queenside space. Rich, dynamic theory.

name: Semi-Slav: Botvinnik System
moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 e6 Bg5 dxc4 e4 b5
description: One of the sharpest openings in chess: Black keeps the extra pawn while White attacks with e5. Deeply analyzed.

name: Semi-Slav: Moscow Variation
moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 e6 Bg5 h6
description: Black asks the bishop's intentions immediately. After Bxf6 Black has the bishop pair and a solid position.

name: Semi-Slav: Marshall Gambit
moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 c6 e4
description: White sacrifices the e-pawn for development and dark-square pressure against the Noteboom/Triangle move order.

name: Catalan Opening
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 g3
description: White combines d4/c4 with a kingside fianchetto, putting long-term pressure on Black's queenside. A favorite of Kramnik and Carlsen.
ideas: Bishop on g2 pressures d5 and b7

name: Catalan Opening: Open Defense
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 g3 d5 Bg2 dxc4
description: Black grabs the c4 pawn; White regains it with Qa4 or Ne5 and keeps pressure on the long diagonal.
ideas: White regains pawn and pressures b7

name: Catalan Opening: Closed
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 g3 d5 Bg2 Be7 Nf3 O-O O-O
description: Black maintains the d5 point; play is slow and positional, with White pressing on the queenside.

name: Indian Defense
moves: d4 Nf6
description: Black develops a knight and controls e4, keeping options for the King's Indian, Nimzo-Indian, Grünfeld and more.

name: Trompowsky Attack
moves: d4 Nf6 Bg5
description: White immediately pins (or threatens to take) the f6 knight, avoiding mainstream Indian theory.
ideas: Damage Black's pawn structure with Bxf6
traps: 2...Ne4 hits the g5 bishop; 3.Bf4 or 3.h4 are the main replies

name: Torre Attack
moves: d4 Nf6 Nf3 e6 Bg5
description: White plays Nf3 and Bg5 with e3, Nbd2 and c3, a solid system with tactical punch.

name: Indian Defense: Normal Variation
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6
description: Black prepares ...d5, ...Bb4 or ...b6, keeping Nimzo-Indian, Queen's Indian and QGD options.

name: Nimzo-Indian Defense
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4
description: Black pins the c3 knight to fight for e4. One of the most respected defenses in chess, rich in strategic ideas.
ideas: Pin the c3 knight to control e4
Give the bishop for doubled pawns

name: Nimzo-Indian: Classical Variation
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Qc2
description: White defends c3 with the queen to recapture without doubled pawns, aiming for the bishop pair.

name: Nimzo-Indian: Rubinstein Variation
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 e3
description: The flexible e3: White develops calmly with Bd3 and Ne2/Nf3, preparing to meet the pin positionally.

name: Nimzo-Indian: Sämisch Variation
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 a3 Bxc3+ bxc3
description: White forces the trade on c3, accepting doubled pawns for the bishop pair and a big center.

name: Nimzo-Indian: Kasparov Variation
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Nf3
description: White develops naturally, often with g3 next, keeping flexibility.

name: Nimzo-Indian: Leningrad Variation
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Bg5
description: White counter-pins the f6 knight, leading to sharp play.

name: Queen's Indian Defense
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 b6
description: Black fianchettoes the queen's bishop to control e4. Solid and flexible, played when White avoids the Nimzo with Nf3.

name: Queen's Indian: Fianchetto Variation
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 b6 g3
description: White counters Black's bishop with his own fianchetto, fighting for the long diagonal.
ideas: Fianchetto battle on the long diagonal

name: Queen's Indian: Petrosian Variation
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 b6 a3
description: White prevents ...Bb4 and prepares Nc3 and d5. Kasparov used it as a powerful weapon.

name: Bogo-Indian Defense
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 Bb4+
description: Black gives a check to trade or misplace White's pieces. Solid and less theoretical than the Nimzo.

name: King's Indian Defense
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6
description: Black fianchettoes and lets White build a big center, planning to strike back with ...e5 or ...c5. Fischer's and Kasparov's weapon.

name: King's Indian Defense: Normal Variation
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6
description: The main King's Indian position: White has a big center and chooses between Classical, Sämisch, Four Pawns and other systems.

name: King's Indian Defense: Classical Variation
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 Nf3 O-O Be2 e5
description: The main line: White develops naturally, Black hits the center with ...e5. Leads to famous race positions.
traps: 8.dxe5 dxe5 9.Qxd8 Rxd8 — the endgame is about equal, not winning for White

name: King's Indian: Mar del Plata Variation
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 Nf3 O-O Be2 e5 O-O Nc6 d5 Ne7
description: The most famous King's Indian line: White attacks on the queenside, Black storms the kingside with ...f5-f4-g5.

name: King's Indian: Petrosian System
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 Nf3 O-O Be2 e5 d5
description: White closes the center immediately with d5, then plays Bg5 to restrain ...f5.

name: King's Indian: Sämisch Variation
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 f3
description: White supports e4 with f3, prepares Be3, Qd2 and often queenside castling with a kingside pawn storm.

name: King's Indian: Four Pawns Attack
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 f4
description: White builds a giant center with four pawns. Black must counter quickly with ...c5 and ...e6.

name: King's Indian: Fianchetto Variation
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nf3 Bg7 g3 O-O Bg2 d6 O-O
description: White fianchettoes too, reducing Black's attacking chances and playing a positional game.

name: King's Indian: Averbakh Variation
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 Be2 O-O Bg5
description: White pins with Bg5 to discourage ...e5 and keep options for h4 attacks.

name: Grünfeld Defense
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5
description: Black lets White build a big center, then attacks it with pieces and ...c5. Dynamic and theory-heavy.

name: Grünfeld: Exchange Variation
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 cxd5 Nxd5 e4 Nxc3 bxc3 Bg7
description: White grabs the center with e4 after trading knights. Black pressures d4 with ...c5, ...Nc6 and ...Bg4.
ideas: Bc4 and Ne2 setup for White

name: Grünfeld: Russian System
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 Nf3 Bg7 Qb3
description: White hits d5 with the queen to force ...dxc4 and then builds the center with e4.

name: Grünfeld: 4.Bf4
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 Bf4
description: White develops the bishop and pressures c7, avoiding the main Exchange lines.

name: Old Indian Defense
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 d6
description: Black plays ...d6 and ...e5 without fianchettoing, leading to solid King's-Indian-like structures.

name: Budapest Gambit
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e5
description: Black gambits the e-pawn for active piece play, often regaining it with ...Ng4. Trappy and fun.
traps: 3.dxe5 Ng4 4.Bf4 Nc6 5.Nf3 Bb4+ 6.Nbd2 Qe7 7.a3 Ngxe5 8.axb4?? Nd3# — famous smothered mate

name: Budapest Gambit: Fajarowicz Variation
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e5 dxe5 Ne4
description: Black places the knight on e4 instead of g4, aiming for quick development and tactics.

name: Modern Benoni
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 e6
description: Black creates an unbalanced structure with a queenside majority against White's central majority. Sharp and dynamic.
traps: The Taimanov Attack with f4 and Bb5+ is very dangerous for Black

name: Modern Benoni: Main Line
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 e6 Nc3 exd5 cxd5 d6 e4 g6
description: The classical Benoni tabiya. White plans e5, Black plays ...a6, ...b5 and ...Re8.

name: Czech Benoni
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 e5
description: Black closes the center with ...e5, aiming for slow maneuvering and ...f5 or ...b5 breaks.

name: Old Benoni
moves: d4 c5
description: Black hits d4 immediately with the c-pawn. After d5, unbalanced Benoni-type positions arise.

name: Benko Gambit
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 b5
description: Black sacrifices a queenside pawn for long-term pressure on the a- and b-files. A great positional gambit.
ideas: Open a- and b-files for rooks

name: Benko Gambit Accepted
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 b5 cxb5 a6 bxa6
description: White takes both pawns. Black recaptures on a6 and gets lasting pressure on the queenside.

name: Dutch Defense
moves: d4 f5
description: Black controls e4 with the f-pawn and aims for a kingside attack. Ambitious but slightly weakening.
traps: 2.Bg5 and 2.e4 (Staunton Gambit) are aggressive anti-Dutch tries
Watch the e8-h5 diagonal — Qh5+ tricks

name: Dutch Defense: Leningrad Variation
moves: d4 f5 c4 Nf6 g3 g6 Bg2 Bg7 Nf3 O-O O-O d6
description: Black combines ...f5 with a King's Indian fianchetto, aiming for ...e5 and a kingside attack.

name: Dutch Defense: Stonewall Variation
moves: d4 f5 c4 Nf6 g3 e6 Bg2 d5 Nf3 c6
description: Black builds a pawn wall on c6-d5-e6-f5, controls e4 and plans a kingside attack.
traps: The e5 hole is a weakness — White puts a knight there

name: Dutch Defense: Classical Variation
moves: d4 f5 c4 Nf6 g3 e6 Bg2 Be7 Nf3 O-O O-O d6
description: Black keeps the d-pawn on d6, preparing ...e5 and ...Qe8-h5.

name: Dutch Defense: Staunton Gambit
moves: d4 f5 e4
description: White strikes at the f5 pawn immediately, offering a pawn for fast development.

name: Englund Gambit
moves: d4 e5
description: A dubious gambit with a famous trap. Black sacrifices e5 for development and tricks.
ideas: Queen to e7 to pressure e5
traps: 2.dxe5 Nc6 3.Nf3 Qe7 4.Bf4? Qb4+ 5.Bd2 Qxb2 6.Bc3?? Bb4! 7.Qd2 Bxc3 8.Qxc3 Qc1# — the famous trap

name: English Opening: Reversed Sicilian
moves: c4 e5
description: White plays a Sicilian with colors reversed, so White has an extra tempo in a Sicilian-like structure.

name: English Opening: Symmetrical Variation
moves: c4 c5
description: Black mirrors White's move. Play is slow and strategic, with many transpositions.

name: English Opening: Four Knights
moves: c4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Nc6
description: All four knights are developed; White plays g3, e3 or d4 to fight for the center.

name: English Opening: Botvinnik System
moves: c4 e5 Nc3 Nc6 g3 g6 Bg2 Bg7 d3 d6 e4
description: White builds a closed structure with pawns on c4, d3 and e4, taking control of d5.

name: English Opening: Anglo-Indian Defense
moves: c4 Nf6
description: Black develops the knight first and keeps options for King's Indian, Nimzo or symmetrical setups.

name: English Opening: Mikenas-Carls Variation
moves: c4 Nf6 Nc3 e6 e4
description: White pushes e4 early, avoiding Nimzo and QGD lines. Sharp and unbalanced.

name: English Opening: Hedgehog
moves: c4 c5 Nf3 Nf6 g3 b6 Bg2 Bb7 O-O e6 Nc3 Be7
description: Black sets up pawns on the 6th rank like a hedgehog's spines, waiting to break with ...b5 or ...d5.

name: English Opening: Agincourt Defense
moves: c4 e6
description: Black prepares ...d5 with a QGD-like setup, or transposes to Nimzo/Queen's Indian structures.

name: Réti Opening: Main Line
moves: Nf3 d5 c4
description: White attacks d5 from the flank, staying in hypermodern style.

name: King's Indian Attack
moves: Nf3 d5 g3
description: White plays a King's Indian setup with an extra tempo: Nf3, g3, Bg2, O-O, d3, Nbd2 and e4. Easy to learn.

name: Bird's Opening: From's Gambit
moves: f4 e5
description: Black sacrifices the e-pawn to open lines against White's weakened king. Very trappy.
traps: 2.fxe5 d6 3.exd6 Bxd6 4.Nf3 g5! threatens ...g4 and ...Bg3#
4.Nc3?? Qh4+ 5.g3 Qxg3+ 6.hxg3 Bxg3# style mates

name: Bird's Opening: Dutch Variation
moves: f4 d5
description: Black takes the center and develops classically. White plays Nf3, e3, b3 and Bb2.
